components.name: Tiered storage (S3) - cold segment offload and backfill reads

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: db.m6i.large — AWS RDS PostgreSQL us-east-1 / On-Demand / Single-AZ (band high = Multi-AZ) / 730 h per month; INSTANCE-HOURS ONLY (excludes storage, provisioned IOPS and backup above the free allocation). Band: deployment spread: low = Single-AZ, high = Multi-AZ. Both are on-demand, standard-tier, us-east-1 PostgreSQL, so the band is fully in scope. Multi-AZ is ~2x Single-AZ.

citations.note: $0.178/h Single-AZ x 730 = 12994c/month. MySQL/MariaDB run ~3.9% cheaper than PostgreSQL for the same class.

assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 200,000 messages/s. 55% produce, 40% hot consume from page cache, 4% backfill replayed from tiered storage, 1% metadata/admin. Messages ~1 KB.

assumptions.subject: broker
assumptions.statement: ~20,000 msg/s per kafka.m5.large broker, counting BOTH produce and consume traffic on the same node. 14 brokers is the binding constraint in this design - which is the correct shape for a Kafka reference: the log, not the clients, is the bottleneck.

assumptions.subject: broker
assumptions.statement: RF=3 means every produced message is written three times inside the cluster. The engine's arrival model counts a client-visible message once, so the broker figure here understates the internal replication write amplification by ~3x on the disk path. Disk/IO capacity is NOT modelled by the v1 analytical engine - size disks from retention x throughput x RF separately.

assumptions.subject: ctrl
assumptions.statement: The KRaft controller quorum is sized for quorum safety (3 nodes), not throughput - it carries only metadata traffic, so its utilisation is low by design.

assumptions.subject: store
assumptions.statement: Consumers commit materialised state in batches of ~20 messages, so the Postgres sink is visited on 5% of consumed messages rather than every one.

assumptions.subject: tier
assumptions.statement: S3 is modelled as 4 prefixes at ~5,500 GET/s each, which is the documented per-prefix request ceiling. Object storage has no per-instance price in Keystone's catalogue, so tiered storage reports $0 compute - the real cost is per-GB-month plus per-request and is a stated GAP here.

assumptions.subject: engine
assumptions.statement: Kafka's defining property is an ORDERED, durable, replayable log with consumer-group offsets. The v1 analytical engine models it as a queueing station with capacity and service time; it cannot express partition ordering, consumer lag, rebalance storms or retention. Those are the failure modes to reason about outside this model.

_library.summary: Partitioned, replicated commit log that decouples producers from consumers at high sustained throughput.
